corrected_content.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $x-3y+z+11=0$ of the plane $\mathrm{Π}$, find an equation of $\mathrm{Π}$ in the form $(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{p})\cdot \mathbf{n}=0.$.
corrected_content.worked_solution:
The coefficients in the Cartesian equation give a normal vector $\mathbf{n}=\langle1,-3,1\rangle$. Setting $x=y=0$ gives $z=-11$, so $P(0,0,-11)$ lies on the plane. Thus,

$$
(\mathbf{r}-\langle0,0,-11\rangle)\cdot\langle1,-3,1\rangle=0.
$$

Expanding recovers the given equation $x-3y+z+11=0$.
